Collect the names into a slice first, since a map has no order to preserve. Then sort that slice with a comparison that looks at the score first and only uses the name when scores are equal. Every tie has to be broken, or the result can change between calls.

Use slices.SortFunc(names, func(a, b string) int { ... }): return cmp.Compare(scores[b], scores[a]) if it isn't 0 (b before a gives highest first), otherwise cmp.Compare(a, b). Return names[:min(n, len(names))].
